alice_support: Escalation from AcmeCorp — after upgrading to py-sdk 1.38 their streaming calls started erroring with a TypeError and they report being charged twice for the same request. Raising to eng for triage. Repro + stack below.

alice_support: Repro (customer-supplied):
```python
# repro.py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
def cb(tok):
    print('tok', tok)
# they used the old arg name 'streaming_callback' which used to work in 1.37
client.generate_stream(model="rw-large", prompt="hello", streaming_callback=cb)
```

alice_support: Stack trace from their job:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 9, in <module>
    client.generate_stream(model="rw-large", prompt="hello", streaming_callback=cb)
TypeError: generate_stream() got an unexpected keyword argument 'streaming_callback'
```

alice_support: Customer says call did not always fail fast; in some runs the call was retried and they were billed twice. Their infra logs show repeated auth refresh and two requests with same payload but different request-ids.

ben_oncall: Do we have the proxied request-ids and region? can you paste the example logs (redwood-proxy)?

alice_support: Pasted redacted log snippet from customer:
```
[2026-01-25T16:02:11Z] req_id=01A2 retry=0 region=us-west-2 status=401 auth=oauth refresh=started
[2026-01-25T16:02:13Z] req_id=01A2 retry=1 region=us-west-2 status=200 auth=oauth refresh=done tokens_charged=123
```

carlos_devex: This rings a bell — 1.38 introduced a kwarg renaming for streaming API (streaming_callback -> on_stream_event) and also changed the request validation flow. In some edge paths an unexpected kwarg is no longer raising synchronously and ends up in the request metric/validator layer which triggers our retry logic. That explains the duplicate requests/billing.

carlos_devex: Quick repro locally: passing an unknown kwarg to generate_stream on 1.38 causes the client to attempt the request instead of raising immediately. On network hiccup it gets retried.

alice_support: Customer wants immediate mitigation and a recommendation to pin.

diana_eng: Confirmed — root cause: we loosened argument validation in the 1.38 client to support passthrough for new features. That inadvertently allowed unknown kwargs to enter the request path instead of failing early. We'll patch to make streaming APIs strict again (fail-fast) and add an explicit deprecation/rename warning.

diana_eng: Short-term mitigation for customers: pin to 1.37.x. Example: `pip install 'redwood-sdk==1.37.*'` or for a specific commit `pip install --force-reinstall 'redwood-sdk==1.37.9'`. Also suggest audit for any uses of `streaming_callback` -> replace with `on_stream_event` and update call sites.

diana_eng: Server-side mitigation we can toggle: disable automatic client retry for streaming endpoints via proxy flag while we push fix (will reduce availability on transient failures but prevents double billing). I'll open a runbook task to toggle and notify SRE.

carlos_devex: I'll prepare a short note for release notes and include example migration snippet:
```python
# 1.37 style
client.generate_stream(..., streaming_callback=my_cb)
# 1.38 -> 1.39 style
client.generate_stream(..., on_stream_event=my_cb)
```

diana_eng: Plan: patch in main to reintroduce strict signature checks + warn on unknown kwarg (hotfix PR targeted for next hour). After hotfix we will cut a 1.38.1 with a deprecation warning and coordinate with support to un-block customers.

deploybot: :construction: created branch hotfix/strict-stream-sigs, PR #1427, CI started, scheduled deploy to staging in 10m.

alice_support: Thanks — I've told AcmeCorp to pin to 1.37 and to avoid retries for now. I'll keep them updated and paste PR link when available. :thumbsup:
